title.zh: 我制作了一个龙骑士VR叙事游戏
title.en: I made a narrative VR game about dragon rider

value.zh:
一点背景信息：这个项目本身是我在布里斯托大学读Immersive Technologies Msc专业的毕业设计（Dissertation）项目，用时大概一个月，团队由两名叙事/3D模型设计师以及两名游戏设计和开发者组成。我在这个团队里担任了这个项目的主要游戏设计和开发工作，以及项目管理。

正如我的课程要求，这是一个VR游戏，但我个人认为这个demo最终呈现出来的完成度和游戏体验对于一个月的设计以及开发时长来说还是可以接受的。我们也为此写了一篇200多页（是的！）的设计论文，但是我不会在这里展示这些，我会尽量精简说明关于这个项目的游戏设计思路和实现过程。

接下来我会分为以下板块，尽量还原我做这个项目的思路和流程，并提炼出有价值的经验：
value.en:
This project was my dissertation project for the MSc in Immersive Technologies at the University of Bristol. It took approximately one month to complete. The team consisted of four members: two narrative and 3D modelling designers, and two game designers and developers. My primary responsibilities were game design, development, and project management.

As required by my course, the project was developed as a VR game. Personally, I think the final demo achieved a reasonable level of polish and delivered a fairly satisfying gameplay experience, especially considering that we only had one month for the entire design and development process.

We also produced a design document of over 200 pages (yes, really!). However, I won't be presenting all of that here. Instead, I'll focus on explaining the key game design ideas and implementation process as concisely as possible.

In the following sections, I'll walk through the project step by step, retracing my design decisions and development process while highlighting the most valuable lessons and insights I gained along the way.

value.zh:
一、立项之初

在我们组建四人团队的时候，关于这个游戏只是一个简单的想法：我们做一款以主角骑龙为核心的游戏怎么样？有时候灵感很重要，但也不必在早期过于纠结想法本身够不够新颖，重点在于围绕这个想法，想要给玩家呈现一个什么样的世界以及带来什么样的体验。围绕这个想法，我们团队开始了头脑风暴，这是为了尽可能地探索游戏形式的边界。我们提出过例如和物理装置（传感器座椅）相连接的真实骑龙模拟器，第一人称开放世界探索，甚至竞速，以及叙事为主的冒险游戏。这个阶段应该尽可能打开自己的思路，尽情畅想，尽管最终只会选择一个方向，但这些思考并不是没有价值的，事实证明，我们最终的demo实际上融合了我们早期的各种想法。

最终想法的敲定来源于多方面的考量。首先是考虑到我们的团队组成，由于我们的团队有两名擅长叙事设计的成员，因此我们认为应该尽可能发挥团队的长处；其次，前期调查，我们综合了沉浸式游戏体验和同类游戏两个方面展开研究，如果用学术方面的语言描述这是在进行背景研究，基于已有的研究结果对细分领域进一步确立方向；如果用游戏行业的语言描述，这是前期竞品分析，目的是将自己的产品做出差异化。但总之，前期调查在初期是必不可少的，因为在这个阶段通过一些文献我们确立了自己的兴趣点，例如玩家的角色认同在VR和PC游戏中的差异、游戏中的道德选项、环境叙事等等。除此之外，关于VR晕动症和模拟器的相关研究也让我们确立了一条优先级最高的设计原则：一切设计都以玩家体验舒适度为大前提。同时我们还发现在现有的VR游戏研究中对于叙事类型和冒险类型的相对缺失，诸如此类。而在同类型游戏中，例如Horizon: Call of the Mountain、Monster Hunter Rise等冒险类，还有一些其他团队开发的VR骑龙早期原型，我们对设计的可取之处进行了参考，也对不合理之处进行反思。同样，这些游戏也对我们的美术风格和世界观产生了不可避免的影响。

最后，来自于专业人士的反馈为我们最终确立方向产生了决定性影响。和行业内以及专业研究人员的讨论让我们意识到，物理装置和研究性方向并不适合我们，并且最终demo的质量和完成度有不容置疑的重要性，一个玩法内容丰富但粗制滥造的VR游戏对于玩家体验来说是毁灭性的；而一个有清晰核心体验，且尽可能降低上手门槛的demo要好得多。

由此，我们最终确立了项目的方向，一个以叙事为主导的VR骑龙冒险游戏。

## 1. Getting the Project Started

When we first formed our team of four, the game was still just a simple idea: What if we made a game centred around riding a dragon?

Sometimes, inspiration is all you need to get started. There is no need to worry too much at such an early stage about whether your idea is original or innovative enough. What matters more is thinking about the kind of world you want to create around that idea and the experience you want to offer players.

With this in mind, we started brainstorming as a team, exploring as many possibilities as possible. We considered a wide range of directions, including a realistic dragon-riding simulator connected to physical equipment such as a motion-sensing seat, a first-person open-world exploration game, a dragon-riding racing game, and even a narrative-driven adventure.

At this stage, I think it is important to keep an open mind and let your imagination run freely. You will eventually have to commit to one direction, but that doesn't mean the other ideas are wasted. In fact, our final demo ended up incorporating elements from several of our early concepts.

Our final direction was shaped by several factors.

First, we considered the strengths of our team. Since two of our members had strong backgrounds in narrative design, we wanted to make the most of those skills rather than pursue a direction that didn't fully utilise our team's strengths.

Second, we conducted some preliminary research, looking at both immersive gaming experiences and games within similar genres. From an academic perspective, this could be described as background research: using existing studies to identify a more specific research direction within a particular field. From a game development perspective, it was essentially competitor analysis, helping us understand the existing market and identify opportunities to differentiate our game.

Whatever you call it, I believe this kind of early research is essential. Through reviewing existing literature, we identified several areas that particularly interested us, including differences in player identification between VR and PC games, moral choices in games, and environmental storytelling.

We also looked into research on VR motion sickness and simulator experiences. This helped us establish what would become our highest-priority design principle: player comfort must come first in every design decision.

At the same time, we noticed that narrative-driven and adventure-focused experiences were relatively underrepresented in existing VR game research. This gave us another reason to explore this direction.

We also studied existing games in similar genres, such as Horizon Call of the Mountain and Monster Hunter Rise, as well as early dragon-riding VR prototypes developed by other teams. We drew inspiration from their successful design choices while also reflecting on aspects that we felt could be improved. Inevitably, these references also influenced our art direction and world-building.

Finally, feedback from industry professionals and academic researchers played a decisive role in shaping our final direction. Discussions with them helped us realise that neither the physical-hardware approach nor a research-focused direction was particularly suitable for our team.

More importantly, we came to understand just how important the quality and overall polish of the final demo would be. A VR game packed with features but poorly executed can be disastrous for the player experience. A much better approach is to build a demo around a clearly defined core experience, while making it as accessible and easy to pick up as possible.

And so, we settled on our final direction: a narrative-driven VR adventure game centred around dragon riding.

二、前期项目管理

在我的另一篇文章中我也曾讨论过项目管理的重要性，作为一个曾经吃过亏的人，我这次在早期阶段就对项目进行了规划。当然，由于时间紧迫，以及团队体量只有4人，所以我只做了精简的规划，以独立开发者的角度。项目管理的工具我只用到了Notion（线上协作文档库）和Github。我在Notion里用Share page将整个项目拆分为几个单独的子页面，如下图所示。

其中以关卡流程和资产需求页面为例，我大多采用表格形式+一行使用说明，尽可能一目了然地让协作者明确如何使用页面进行管理，如下图所示。值得一提的是其中关卡流程里直接将流程拆分成具体事件名，这样在之后的开发中构建事件集合（EventBus）更加方便。同样的，对于资产我也要求统一补充具体资产上传的路径，这样对于开发者来说可以方便地定位。

其中项目管理这一页是我简单划分的时间线图，如下面所示，但实际上在早期无需过于精确，只要有大致项目节点的概念即可，更为细致的划分我直接在Github中进行管理。大致的节点应包含早期demo，内部测试（Alpha Test），Debug和改进阶段，外部测试（Beta Test），在实际开发中，会进行多次内部测试，后期则进行多次外部测试。

在Github中，我创建仓库后让每个成员单独创建个人分支，并且设置了下一节点日期的里程碑。并且通过issue board来管理我和另一名开发者的具体开发任务。每次的流程都是我们各自在分支上进行开发，验证无误后合并到主干上，避免出现混乱。

此外，我们还有定期会议，及时同步各自的贡献以及帮助他人解决问题，明确之后的工作内容。
value.en:
2. Early-stage Project Management
In another article, I also discussed the importance of project management. Having learned this lesson the hard way in the past, I made sure to plan the project from the very beginning this time.

Of course, given our tight schedule and small team of just four people, I kept the planning relatively lightweight, taking an approach closer to that of an indie developer rather than introducing a complicated management process.

The only project management tools I used were Notion (for online documentation and collaboration) and GitHub.

In Notion, I used the Share page feature to divide the project into several individual subpages, as shown below.
Notion project structureFor example, the Level Flow and Asset Requirements pages were primarily organised using tables, each accompanied by a short line of instructions. My goal was to make everything as clear and straightforward as possible, so that every team member could immediately understand how to use each page to manage their work.

One detail worth mentioning is that, in the Level Flow page, I broke the entire progression down into individual events, each with a specific event name. This made it much easier to organise and implement the event collection (EventBus) during later development.

Similarly, for asset management, I required everyone to provide the exact upload path for each asset. This allowed developers to locate the corresponding files quickly without having to search through the project manually.
Level Flow and Asset Requirements pagesThe Project Management page contained a simple timeline outlining the major project milestones, as shown below. In practice, however, there is no need to make this timeline overly detailed at such an early stage. Having a general understanding of the key milestones is usually enough. I managed the more detailed task breakdown directly through GitHub.

Our main milestones included:
- Early Demo: Getting an initial playable version ready.
- Internal Testing (Alpha Test): Testing the game within the team.
- Debugging and Improvements: Fixing issues and refining the experience.
- External Testing (Beta Test): Getting feedback from people outside the development team.
During actual development, we conducted multiple rounds of internal testing, followed by several rounds of external testing towards the later stages of the project.
Project timeline in NotionOn GitHub, I created a repository and asked each team member to work on their own individual branch. I also set up milestones based on the deadlines for our upcoming development stages.

For day-to-day development, I used the GitHub Issue Board to manage specific tasks for myself and the other developer.

Our workflow was straightforward: we each worked independently on our own branches, tested and verified our changes, and then merged them into the main branch once everything was working as expected. This helped us avoid unnecessary conflicts and kept the project organised.

Finally, we held regular team meetings to share progress, keep everyone updated on individual contributions, help each other resolve problems, and agree on what needed to be done next.

Overall, I found that a lightweight but clearly structured management process was more than enough for a small team working under a tight deadline. The key was not to create more management overhead, but to make sure everyone knew what they were responsible for, where to find the information they needed, and what the next milestone was.

三、玩法核心及测试

整个游戏的概念核心就是骑龙。因此我在设计时需要确保其它系统都围绕着这个核心展开。因此在早期开发阶段，最值得细致打磨和反复验证的阶段就是确保骑龙这个玩法本身成立。因此我一开始只搭建了一个简单场景，在这个场景中玩家可以体验到召唤龙→骑乘→地面骑行和空中飞行的控制方式→降落，并且在第一版操作方式实现之后立刻展开了内部和小规模外部测试，事实证明这样做是很有价值的。在第一版方案中，玩家可以通过手臂摆动和控制器上按钮一同控制，这样做一方面是为了真实身体控制带来的沉浸感，另一方面是由于考虑到玩家对游戏设备的熟练度不同，为了降低操作门槛引入了控制器按钮+游戏内高亮按键引导。然而，在实际的用户测试中，我们收到了以下反馈，对我们的设计迭代影响重大：

1. 骑龙感觉不够真实。
2. 没有掌控任何生物的感觉。
3. 手臂运动检测过于灵敏。
4. 巨龙转向过于频繁，带来不适感。

除此之外，还有建议提到，我们应该对玩家跟随龙一起垂直移动的幅度做出调整；玩家低头查看时，发现距离龙背的距离太远，不符合骑龙的真实感等等。除了小部分由于开发时长限制最终无法实现的建议外（例如有人建议我们应该增加自定义设置选项，允许玩家自定是否跟随龙的动作频率，以及操作控制等）大部分的建议我们都采纳并且进行了迭代。
value.en:
## 3. Core Gameplay Design and Testing

The core concept of the entire game was dragon riding. Therefore, I wanted to make sure that every other system was designed around this central experience.

During the early stages of development, the most important thing to focus on was making sure that dragon riding itself actually worked as a gameplay experience. This meant spending time refining and repeatedly testing the core mechanics before moving on to other systems.

I started by building a simple test environment where players could experience the complete dragon-riding sequence:

Summoning the dragon → Mounting → Ground movement and flight controls → Landing.

As soon as the first version of the controls was implemented, I immediately started internal testing and small-scale external playtesting. Looking back, this was one of the most valuable decisions we made during development.

In the initial version, players could control the dragon using a combination of arm movements and controller buttons. There were two main reasons behind this approach.

First, I wanted to use physical arm movements to create a greater sense of immersion through natural body interaction. Second, I wanted to accommodate players with different levels of familiarity with VR equipment. To lower the learning curve, I introduced controller buttons alongside highlighted button prompts within the game to guide players through the controls.

However, our user testing revealed several issues that had a significant impact on our subsequent design iterations:

1. Dragon riding did not feel realistic enough.
2. Players did not feel like they were actually controlling a living creature.
3. Arm movement detection was too sensitive.
4. The dragon turned too frequently, causing discomfort.

We also received several additional suggestions. For example, testers recommended adjusting how much the player's body moved vertically in response to the dragon's movement. Some players also noticed that when looking down, the distance between their body and the dragon's back was too great, breaking the illusion of actually riding a dragon.

Apart from a few suggestions that we ultimately couldn't implement due to development time constraints, we adopted and iterated on most of the feedback.

For instance, some testers suggested adding customisation options that would allow players to independently adjust how closely their body followed the dragon's movements, as well as customise the control scheme. Although we recognised the value of these suggestions, we had to prioritise the improvements that would have the greatest impact on the overall experience within our limited development time.

value.zh:
在第二版控制方案中，我曾经考虑过手势识别。然而这个方案并未实现，原因主要有三：一、手势控制会损失控制器震动带来的反馈感。二、手势与控制器混合控制过于复杂，而全部使用手势进行控制则与游戏内大量交互需求冲突，做相应调整将带来无法预估的工作量。三、手势控制对于用户来说学习成本剧增，为了普适性，我们最终放弃了这一方案。

最后的方案里，我提议让美术成员制作了龙鞍的模型，然后我增加了一副有缰绳连接的握把，让玩家可以在游戏内抓握握把，并且移动手臂方向和距离对龙进行控制。这种设计有三个主要优势：

一、在这个方案中，我将空间中的玩家控制器的1/2处作为中心（约为玩家胸口位置），向上下左右前后六个方向延申指定距离后，形成一个可供检测的平面（平面大小和距离都可以自定义），再由平面中心延伸出一段深度检测距离。当且仅当玩家抓着握把进入某个检测平面后才会触发对应方向的控制操作，而穿过平面的深度则决定了控制强度。这样做的好处是解决了之前初版方案中，玩家只要有身体移动就会触发控制操作和控制精度需求之间的冲突，这也是之前测试中导致用户感觉转向太灵敏的原因。

二、使用虚拟握把接管驾驶龙的全部操作，解放了原本绑定的控制器按键，这为其他交互需求提供了空间。

三、游戏内握把方向和缰绳紧绷程度全部可视化，并且有不同程度的控制器震动反馈，让玩家体感更真实的同时，也更易于上手。

值得一提的是，我还增加了甩动握把触发挥鞭加速的操作指令，让骑乘体验更贴合现实。

关于平面检测的模型，以及缰绳如何模拟真实物理等实现细节，感兴趣的话可以联系我的邮箱，在此处不展开赘述。
value.en:
For the second iteration of the control scheme, I also considered introducing gesture recognition. However, this approach was never implemented, mainly for three reasons.

1. Loss of haptic feedback: Gesture-based controls would sacrifice the tactile feedback provided by controller vibrations.
2. Interaction complexity: Combining gestures with controller inputs would make the control scheme unnecessarily complicated. On the other hand, relying entirely on gestures would conflict with the large number of other interactions required throughout the game. Adapting the entire interaction system would introduce an unpredictable amount of additional work.
3. Learning curve: Gesture-based controls would significantly increase the learning curve for players. Since accessibility and ease of use were important priorities, we eventually decided to abandon this approach.

For the final solution, I suggested that our art team create a 3D model of a dragon saddle. I then added a pair of virtual handles connected to the saddle by reins. Players could grab these handles in-game and control the dragon by changing the direction and distance of their arm movements.

This design offered three major advantages.

1\. More precise and reliable movement detection.

I designed a spatial detection system using the midpoint between the player's two controllers as its centre (approximately corresponding to the player's chest position).

From this centre, I extended configurable distances in six directions: up, down, left, right, forward, and backward. This created a set of detection planes, with both their size and distance from the centre adjustable. Each plane also had an additional depth detection range extending outwards from its centre.

The key principle was that directional controls would only be triggered when the player was holding the virtual handles and moving them into the corresponding detection plane. The depth of penetration into the plane then determined the intensity of the control input.

This solved a major problem with the initial control scheme: previously, almost any body movement could trigger a control input, making it difficult to balance natural movement with precise control. This was also one of the main reasons testers found the dragon's turning behaviour too sensitive.

2\. Freeing up controller inputs for other interactions.

By transferring all dragon-piloting controls to the virtual handles, I was able to free up the controller buttons that had previously been dedicated to flying the dragon. This left more room for other gameplay interactions without creating conflicts between different control inputs.

3\. Better visual and haptic feedback.

The direction of the virtual handles and the tension of the reins were both visualised in-game. Different levels of controller vibration were also introduced to reflect the intensity of the player's inputs.

This not only made the experience feel more realistic, but also helped players understand how their movements affected the dragon, making the controls easier to learn.

One additional detail worth mentioning is that I also introduced a whip-cracking acceleration command. Players could flick the handles to make the dragon accelerate, making the riding experience feel even closer to its real-world counterpart.

There are also some more technical details behind the detection-plane system and how the reins simulate realistic physical behaviour. If you're interested in learning more about the implementation, feel free to contact me via email. I'll leave those details out of this article for now.

除了玩家控制操作方面的迭代，在这一阶段我还做了一个很重要的早期决定：将玩家和龙的移动完全分离。最初版本里，最直接的做法是将玩家对象置于龙对象层级下，让玩家完全跟随龙的移动。这是因为在现实中，骑乘者随骑乘对象一同移动是符合逻辑的。然而，在测试中我们发现，这对于VR来说有很大造成不适感的风险，并且，对于第一人称游戏的视觉表现来说，龙的移动幅度需要考虑不遮挡玩家视野的同时，做到尽量真实，例如垂直方向的振翅和转向时倾斜；而玩家若完全跟随龙的动作，会涉及到强行调整玩家双眼位置，这是VR晕动症的主要来源之一。因此，在最终的实现中，玩家仅在垂直方向上有小量幅度的移动，而在转向时完全不倾斜。为了弥补这一部分的真实感，我做出了以下几项体验优化：

1. 音频：风声随着风速的增加而增强，并伴有翅膀拍打声、龙鸣声等。
2. 风粒子：一个放置在玩家双眼正前方的锥形粒子生成区域，只在骑行时触发，随速度增加粒子密度。
3. 周边视野遮挡和模糊：随速度增加和转向角度加大，视野会缩小，周边光流减少，从而降低晕动风险。
4. 控制器的震动反馈：不同的操作带来不同程度的震动反馈，例如甩鞭时，速度增大时。

最终的版本进行公开测试后，现场没有任何一个用户感到不适，并且体验者包含大量不熟悉VR和游戏的用户，他们都能短时间内迅速理解操作逻辑并享受乐趣。当然，这也离不开我在后期阶段主要打磨的引导系统，但这也反映了一个重要经验：越是核心的玩法，越应该在早期进行优先开发和测试，在体验完善之前不要贸然进入下一步。
value.en:
Beyond refining the player controls, I made another important design decision at this stage: completely separating the player's movement from the dragon's movement.

In the initial version, the most straightforward approach was to place the player object under the dragon object's hierarchy, allowing the player to follow the dragon's movements directly. From a real-world perspective, this made perfect sense: when riding an animal, the rider naturally moves along with it.

However, our testing revealed that this approach could create significant discomfort in VR.

There were two main issues to consider. First, from a first-person visual perspective, the dragon's movements needed to look as realistic as possible without obstructing the player's view. This included vertical movements caused by wing flapping and body tilting during turns.

Second, if the player completely followed the dragon's movements, we would have to forcibly adjust the position of the player's eyes to match the dragon's movements. This is one of the major potential causes of VR motion sickness.

Therefore, in the final implementation, the player's body only follows the dragon with a small amount of vertical movement, while remaining completely level during turns, without any tilting.

Of course, this meant sacrificing some physical realism. To compensate for that, I introduced several additional features to improve the overall experience:

1. Audio: Wind sounds become louder as the flying speed increases, accompanied by wing-flapping sounds and dragon roars.
2. Wind particles: I created a cone-shaped particle emission area positioned directly in front of the player's eyes. It is only activated while riding, with particle density increasing alongside the dragon's speed.
3. Peripheral vision reduction and blur: As speed increases and turning angles become larger, the player's field of view gradually narrows, reducing peripheral visual motion and helping minimise the risk of motion sickness.
4. Controller haptic feedback: Different actions produce different levels of controller vibration, including cracking the reins to accelerate and increasing the dragon's speed.

After the final version was released for public testing, none of the participants experienced discomfort during the sessions. This was particularly encouraging because many of them had little or no previous experience with VR or video games. Nevertheless, they were able to quickly understand the controls and enjoy the experience.

Of course, this was also partly thanks to the guidance system that I spent much of the later development stage refining.

However, I think this process demonstrates an important lesson: the more central a gameplay mechanic is to your game, the earlier you should develop and test it. Don't rush into building additional systems before the core experience is properly established.

四、叙事为骨，生长出玩法和副系统

在开发龙的驾驶操作时，我跟进了几次叙事组的会议，结合来自专业脚本设计师的建议，我们最终在这个阶段敲定了整个游戏的叙事剧本。

在最终剧本完成前，我并没有贸然开展更复杂的玩法和系统设计。这是因为在我看来，一个叙事为核心的游戏，任何玩法都应该为叙事服务，玩法不应该打断叙事节奏，且和剧情割裂。所以，在拿到完整剧本后，我立刻对整个剧本进行分析，拆解出完整流程，划分节点，然后在梳理的过程中对玩法和系统进行构思。

## 4. Building Gameplay and Supporting Systems Around the Narrative

While working on the dragon controls, I also attended several meetings with the narrative team. With additional feedback and suggestions from a professional scriptwriter, we eventually finalised the complete game script at this stage.

Before the final script was ready, I deliberately avoided moving ahead with more complex gameplay and system design.

My reasoning was simple: in a narrative-driven game, gameplay should always serve the story. It should neither interrupt the narrative flow nor feel disconnected from the events taking place in the game.

Once I received the complete script, I immediately started analysing it. I broke down the entire narrative into a complete sequence of events, identified the key progression points, and mapped out the overall game flow.

As I worked through the script and organised its structure, I began developing ideas for gameplay mechanics and supporting systems that could naturally emerge from the narrative itself.

- 玩家与龙

首先，剧本给我带来最重要的一个启发（也是该项目的亮点）是龙与玩家的关系。在故事中，玩家全程骑行的龙并不单纯是一个坐骑，而是主角一同成长的伙伴。而在大量同类游戏中，龙多数被设定为一个坐骑，坐骑本身也可以获得成长，但如何让玩家感受到伙伴之间的羁绊，则是一个在玩法方面值得探索的方向。

在设计龙和玩家之间如何互动时，我希望这不仅仅是装饰性的，而是能对整个游戏产生影响的机制。但我不希望给玩家带来任何“逼迫感”或者这种影响会导致游戏流程卡住，因此在平衡情感体验和游戏性时，我主要遇到了以下三个方面的设计挑战：（以下内容引用自我的论文）

### Player and Dragon

First, the most important inspiration I drew from the script (and one of the project's key highlights) was the relationship between the dragon and the player.

In the story, the dragon that the player rides throughout the game is not simply a mount. It is a companion that grows alongside the protagonist. In many similar games, dragons are primarily treated as mounts. While these mounts may have their own progression and development systems, creating a genuine sense of emotional connection between the player and their companion is a much more interesting design challenge worth exploring through gameplay.

When designing the interactions between the player and the dragon, I wanted this relationship to be more than just a visual or decorative element. It needed to be a meaningful mechanic that could influence the overall game experience.

However, I also wanted to avoid making players feel forced to interact with the dragon, or allowing the relationship system to prevent them from progressing through the game.

Balancing emotional engagement with gameplay therefore presented three major design challenges:

(The following sections are quoted from my dissertation.)

value.zh:
一、当没有人给龙下指令时，龙会做什么？

当没有指令时，一辆载具会沉默，但对于一个活生生的生物来说，它应当具备某种自主意识。最直接的做法是使用单个状态机，例如空闲、行走、睡觉或者被骑乘，事件负责切换这些状态。这看似合理，然而对生物来说却是错误的设计。这是因为单个状态机无法表达一个真实生物具备的两个方面：第一，它无法让自身的真实需求决定行为的优先级。状态机回答的是“我正在做什么，以及接下来可以做什么？”，但它没有地方存储“我有多累，以及距离上一次有人关注我已经过去多久？”因此，这些转换只能被编写为状态之间的条件，而各种动机之间的优先级则分散在所有可能进入这些状态的地方，而不是作为一个可以被读取、调整和推理的对象而存在。每当添加一种新的动机时，就必须重新检查所有现有状态的退出条件。因此，系统的增长并不是线性的，而是趋向于乘法式增长。这对于模拟生物体的决策行为而言，既不稳定，也难以维护。

第二，它的自主行为可能会成为游戏流程推进的障碍。这是一个我最初低估的需求，也是“生物（creature）”与“捣乱者（troublemaker）”之间最关键的区别。龙有自己的冲动：它会感到疲倦、渴望得到关注，也会四处游荡。与此同时，游戏中也包含精心安排的时刻：某个角色可能正在说话，玩家可能正在等待完成某个教程操作，或者剧情可能要求龙以特定的姿势躺下。如果自主行为能够打断这些时刻，那么游戏中每一段预先安排好的内容都会变得脆弱。某个环节是否会出错，取决于龙在那个时刻恰好有多疲倦，这使得问题变得难以复现。

因此，真正的需求并不只是“龙应该具有自主行为”，而是：

龙的自主行为必须能够与外部事件进行优先级比较，并且能够被优先级更高的游戏内容覆盖。

经过多次迭代，我最终采用了一个三层结构（如下图），将龙的需求、行为决策和具体行动分开处理。

### 1. What Does the Dragon Do When Nobody Gives It Instructions?

When no one gives a vehicle any instructions, it simply remains idle. But a living creature should have some degree of autonomy of its own.

The most straightforward approach would be to use a single state machine, with states such as Idle, Walking, Sleeping, and Mounted, and events responsible for switching between them.

This might seem reasonable at first, but it turns out to be the wrong approach when simulating a living creature.

There are two main reasons for this.

First, a single state machine cannot use the creature's actual needs to determine behavioural priorities.

A state machine answers the questions: "What am I doing right now, and what can I do next?" But it has nowhere to store information such as "How tired am I?" or "How long has it been since someone last paid attention to me?"

As a result, transitions can only be implemented as conditions between states. The priorities between different motivations end up scattered across all the places where those states can be entered, rather than existing as something that can be independently accessed, adjusted, and reasoned about.

Every time a new motivation is introduced, all existing state exit conditions need to be reviewed again. This means the complexity of the system does not grow linearly, but tends towards multiplicative growth.

For simulating the decision-making behaviour of a living creature, this approach is neither stable nor easy to maintain.

Second, the creature's autonomous behaviour can become an obstacle to game progression.

This was a requirement I initially underestimated, and it is perhaps the most important distinction between a creature and a troublemaker.

The dragon has its own impulses. It gets tired, wants attention, and wanders around. At the same time, the game contains carefully orchestrated moments: a character might be speaking, the player might be waiting to complete a tutorial action, or the narrative might require the dragon to lie down in a specific pose.

If autonomous behaviour is allowed to interrupt these moments, every carefully scripted sequence becomes fragile. Whether something goes wrong could depend entirely on how tired the dragon happens to be at that particular moment, making issues extremely difficult to reproduce and debug.

Therefore, the actual requirement was not simply that "the dragon should behave autonomously", but rather:

The dragon's autonomous behaviours must be able to compete with external events in terms of priority, while also allowing higher-priority game content to override them.

After several iterations, I eventually settled on a three-layer architecture (shown below), separating the dragon's needs, behavioural decision-making, and actual actions.

value.zh:
最底层是龙的需求（Needs），用数值记录龙当前的状态。耐力（Stamina）会因骑行、飞行和战斗而消耗，但不会随着时间自然下降，避免玩家无法理解耐力变化的原因。心情（Mood）则会随着玩家长时间不与龙互动而下降。

最初，我还加入了饥饿值（Hunger），但后来将其删除。如果不同需求都要求玩家采取不同的照料行为，就会频繁打断游戏流程。因此，我让喂食和抚摸都能恢复耐力和心情，只是恢复的数值不同。这样既保留了互动选择，也避免了不必要的打扰。

中间层是仲裁层（Arbitration），负责决定龙应该做什么。它首先按照优先级筛选行为：玩家指令最高，其次是生存需求、寻求关注，最后是待机行为。然后，再根据龙当前的需求状态，为同一优先级下的行为评分，并选择得分最高的一个。

仅有优先级分组还不够。如果系统只按照固定优先级选择行为，龙就会永远执行当前最重要的事情，行为也会变得过于刻板和可预测。因此，我在每个优先级组内加入了评分机制。当龙同时有些疲倦、又有些孤独时，它可以根据当前需求选择不同的行为，而不是每次都做出完全相同的决定。这种适度的不确定性，让玩家感觉龙有自己的想法，而不只是在执行固定规则。

最顶层是行为状态机（Action State Machine），负责执行具体动作。每个状态都有自己的中断规则：可以立即中断、需要完成当前动画后再中断，或者完全不能中断。例如，虽然玩家指令拥有最高优先级，但如果龙正在飞行，玩家突然要求它躺下，立即切换状态就会破坏动作表现。因此，玩家指令的高优先级并不意味着所有动作都必须立即中断，而是需要结合当前动作的中断规则来执行。
value.en:
The bottom layer consists of the dragon's Needs, which use numerical values to represent its current condition.

Stamina is consumed through riding, flying, and combat, but does not naturally decrease over time. This avoids situations where players cannot understand why their dragon's stamina is dropping.

Mood, on the other hand, gradually decreases when the player goes for a long time without interacting with the dragon.

Initially, I also introduced a Hunger value, but eventually decided to remove it. If different needs required players to perform different care activities, these interactions would frequently interrupt the flow of gameplay. Instead, I made both feeding and petting restore stamina and mood, although the amount restored differs between the two actions.

This preserved some variety in player interactions without introducing unnecessary interruptions.

The middle layer is the Arbitration Layer, which determines what the dragon should do.

It first filters available behaviours according to their priority:

1. Player commands
2. Survival needs
3. Seeking attention
4. Idle behaviours

It then evaluates behaviours within the same priority group based on the dragon's current needs and selects the one with the highest score.

However, simply grouping behaviours by priority is not enough. If the system always selects behaviours based on a fixed priority order, the dragon will keep performing whatever is currently considered the most important activity. Its behaviour will eventually become rigid and overly predictable.

To address this, I introduced a scoring mechanism within each priority group. For example, when the dragon is both somewhat tired and somewhat lonely, the system can evaluate its current needs and choose between different behaviours, rather than making exactly the same decision every time.

This degree of variation introduces a little unpredictability, helping players feel that the dragon has a mind of its own rather than simply following a set of predefined rules.

The top layer is the Action State Machine, which handles the execution of specific actions.

Each state has its own interruption rules. An action can be interrupted immediately, only after its current animation finishes, or cannot be interrupted at all.

For example, even though player commands have the highest priority, imagine that the dragon is currently flying and the player suddenly asks it to lie down. Switching states immediately would break the animation and make the behaviour look unnatural.

Therefore, giving player commands the highest priority does not mean that every ongoing action must be interrupted immediately. The system must also consider the interruption rules of the current action before executing a new command.

二、玩家如何感知到关系发生了变化？

只通过文字或者剧情告诉玩家这一点虽然简单，但很单薄。我最初的做法是一个双轴模型：第一根轴是性格，从凶猛到温顺，它受到玩家剧情选项的影响；另一根轴是信任度，通过玩家与龙的交互行为逐渐获得提升。龙在游戏中的表现受到双轴的共同影响，例如响应玩家指令的速度，信任度高时，它会立即服从；信任度低时，它可能会犹豫，部分服从。

但这一方案在初期就遇到了困难，一方面是性格轴带来了无法预估的巨大工作量，不同的动画表现，对战斗系统的影响，甚至不同的剧情分支等等，由于团队规模和时间限制，我们无法全部实现。而且，我们无法保证这种性格变化的表现一定能够被玩家感知，一个无法被衡量的机制还不如不存在。另一方面是信任度机制的失败，这是因为这个机制给玩家带来的全是负反馈，例如，当龙处于低信任度而没有响应玩家召唤时，比起让玩家感受到是信任不足，更可能让玩家觉得这是一个游戏bug。而我们设计这一部分的初衷是让玩家感受到和伙伴的共同成长。

在最终方案的迭代中，我将性格轴移除，将信任轴直接作为推进游戏流程的轴线，具体来说，玩家会随着信任提升而解锁更多骑龙操控的能力，以及更多游戏内容。这在逻辑上是合理的，毕竟一条不够信任你的龙，可能不会允许你骑着它飞行。此外，对于大多数玩家来说，可能从未使用过VR，而游戏内包含大量需要学习的操作，成长路线的设置也提供了一个循序渐进的学习过程，减轻了玩家一开始就要面对大量操作的压力。

这一设计也服务于游戏叙事，让玩家能够从游戏世界中自然理解成长过程。

在大多数游戏中，能力解锁通常通过 UI 提示来解释。但在我们的游戏中，玩家需要收集材料、制作更好的装备，并在这个过程中骑着龙四处探索。随着龙对玩家的信任增加，再配合新装备，玩家便能自然解锁更多能力。因此，信任值（Trust）是永久且分阶段提升的，一旦解锁飞行能力，就不会再失去。而耐力（Stamina）和心情（Mood）则是实时变化的，它们决定龙当前是否愿意带玩家行动。例如，即使龙已经非常信任玩家，如果一整个下午都在飞行且没有得到照料，它仍然会因为太累而拒绝再次起飞。

这两类数值结合起来，才让照料真正成为游戏中的必要行为，而不只是让玩家感觉自己与龙关系很好。信任决定玩家是否获得某项能力，而耐力和心情决定玩家今天是否照顾好了龙。如果玩家忽视龙，旅程就会因此中断。当玩家理解原因并主动喂食时，这个互动过程本身就能传达玩家与龙之间的关系变化，而不需要额外增加任何对话。
value.en:
### 2. How Can Players Perceive Changes in Their Relationship with the Dragon?

Simply telling players through dialogue or narrative that their relationship with the dragon has changed is easy to implement, but it feels rather superficial. I wanted the relationship to be reflected in the actual gameplay experience.

My initial approach was to introduce a two-axis model.

The first axis represented Personality, ranging from Aggressive to Gentle. It was influenced by the player's choices throughout the story.

The second axis represented Trust, which gradually increased through interactions between the player and the dragon.

The dragon's behaviour would be influenced by both axes. For example, they would affect how quickly the dragon responded to player commands. With high trust, the dragon would obey immediately; with low trust, it might hesitate or only partially follow the command.

However, this approach ran into problems quite early in development.

On the one hand, the Personality axis introduced an enormous amount of additional work that was difficult to estimate. Different animation behaviours, potential impacts on the combat system, and even alternative narrative branches would all need to be considered. Given our team size and limited development time, implementing all of these features was simply unrealistic.

More importantly, we couldn't guarantee that players would actually notice these personality changes. A mechanic that cannot be clearly perceived or evaluated by players might as well not exist.

On the other hand, the Trust system also had a fundamental problem: it primarily generated negative feedback for players.

For example, if the dragon had low trust and refused to respond to a summoning command, players were more likely to interpret this as a game bug than as an indication that the dragon did not trust them enough.

This was the opposite of what we originally wanted. Our intention was to let players experience the feeling of growing together with their companion, rather than making them feel punished for having a poor relationship.

In the final iteration, I removed the Personality axis and turned Trust directly into a progression system.

More specifically, as trust increases, players gradually unlock additional dragon-riding abilities and access to more game content.

From a narrative perspective, this makes sense. After all, a dragon that does not fully trust you might not be willing to let you ride it while flying.

There is also an important gameplay benefit. Many players may have little or no previous VR experience, and our game involves quite a few controls and interactions that need to be learned. By tying ability unlocks to relationship progression, we could introduce these mechanics gradually instead of overwhelming players with too many controls right from the beginning.

This design also supports the narrative by allowing players to understand their progression naturally through the game world.

In most games, newly unlocked abilities are usually explained through UI notifications. However, in our game, players need to collect materials, craft better equipment, and explore the world on their dragon throughout this process.

As the dragon gradually develops trust in the player, new equipment and increased trust work together to unlock additional abilities.

This led to an important distinction between our two types of relationship values:

- Trust: A permanent, staged progression value. Once an ability such as flying is unlocked, it will never be taken away.
- Stamina and Mood: Dynamic values that change in real time and determine whether the dragon is currently willing to accompany the player.

For example, even if the dragon fully trusts the player, it might still refuse to take off if it has spent the entire afternoon flying without receiving any care and has become exhausted.

Combining these two types of values is what makes caring for the dragon a meaningful part of the gameplay, rather than simply giving players the impression that they have a good relationship.

Trust determines what the player has earned the ability to do, while Stamina and Mood determine whether the dragon is currently in a condition to do it.

If players neglect their dragon, their journey will eventually be interrupted. When they understand why this happens and actively choose to feed or care for the dragon, the interaction itself communicates how their relationship works and changes over time, without requiring any additional dialogue.

value.zh:
三、如何让信任不成为游戏流程的阻碍

让信任值（Trust）决定游戏进度，也带来了一个新问题：如果信任和照料决定玩家能够做什么，那么不够细心的玩家就可能被卡在游戏中。对于一款叙事驱动的游戏来说，这是无法接受的。为此，我在不同的游戏进度阶段加入了补偿机制。如果玩家的信任值低于当前剧情阶段的预期，龙的内部状态机就会更频繁地触发与自身需求相关的行为，提醒玩家注意照料龙。这个机制在后台自动运行，玩家不需要察觉它的存在，但可以避免因为忘记照料龙而无法继续游戏。

此外，为了避免滚雪球效应，信任值只通过玩家主动进行的行为来增加，例如：抚摸、喂食、累计骑行时间、剧情奖励。

至此，游戏中最核心的龙系统正式完成，当然，在实际的开发过程中，这个系统都在不断测试和迭代，我同步还在进行着其他系统的实现。例如，在我完成龙的基本驾驶控制和对象分离后，我就将战斗操作的实现交给了组内另一名开发人员负责，而我则继续专注在决定了整个游戏流程的关卡系统上。
value.en:
### 3. How to Prevent Trust from Becoming a Progression Blocker

Making Trust responsible for game progression introduced another problem: if trust and caring determine what players can do, less attentive players might eventually get stuck.

For a narrative-driven game, this is simply unacceptable.

To address this, I introduced a compensation mechanism at different stages of game progression.

If the player's Trust value falls below the expected level for the current narrative stage, the dragon's internal state machine will trigger behaviours related to its own needs more frequently. These behaviours serve as reminders for players to pay attention to the dragon and take care of it.

This mechanism runs automatically in the background. Players don't need to know that it exists, but it helps prevent them from becoming unable to progress simply because they have forgotten to care for their dragon.

I also wanted to avoid a snowball effect, so Trust can only increase through deliberate player actions, such as:

- Petting the dragon.
- Feeding the dragon.
- Accumulating riding time.
- Receiving narrative progression rewards.

With this, the core dragon system was finally complete.

Of course, throughout actual development, the system continued to undergo testing and iteration. Meanwhile, I was also working on other gameplay systems.

For example, once I had completed the basic dragon controls and separated the player's movement from the dragon's, I handed over the implementation of the combat controls to another developer on the team. I then continued focusing on the level system, which ultimately determined the progression and overall structure of the game.

- 关卡

关卡系统可以说是整个项目的数据结构核心，因此在进行代码工作之前，我首先对照整个剧本对关卡入口和结束的节点做出了划分，并且设计了每一部分单独的任务（目标）和玩法。（如下图所示）

首先从类型上，整个流程的组成可以分为剧情演出、教学和玩家自主行动阶段。对于玩法来说，在剧情演出阶段，我选择了部分节点插入了剧情分支选项，其中分为会对游戏内容造成影响和对游戏内容无影响仅对话表现不同两种类型。而大部分玩法集中在玩家自主行动阶段，例如采集任务，战斗，天空竞速赛等等。

在拆分完整个流程事件结构后，我在关卡设计的事件表中将所有单独事件名按类型列出，然后在事件表的基础上,我将整个流程在代码层面抽象为三类容器,分别对应前面划分的三种阶段:

教学阶段对应"步骤"(Step)。每个步骤包含触发条件、呈现内容(文字提示、按钮高亮、旁白等)、完成条件和下一步。它的特点是只在玩家真正完成动作后才推进,不依赖任何计时,以保证教学不会"自己往前走"。剧情演出阶段对应"叙述序列"(Narration Sequence)与"对话"(Dialogue)。叙述序列是一条按时间推进的演出时间线,可以携带淡入淡出、传送、角色动画等指令;对话则是节点图结构,每个节点包含台词、可选的分支选项和选择后的效果。两者的区分依据是"谁在说话、从哪里说":旁白与主角内心独白属于叙述序列,场景中真实存在的角色发言属于对话。玩家自主行动阶段对应"目标"(Objective)与首次发生的"提示"(Beat)。采集、战斗、竞速等玩法各自独立实现,只通过事件告知流程"目标已更新或已完成",流程系统本身不包含任何玩法逻辑。

所有这些容器之间不直接引用,而是统一通过核心层的事件总线通信。玩法模块发布事件(例如"玩家完成传送"”物品放入背包"”敌人被击败"),信号路由器把它们翻译成统一的信号,步骤机订阅信号并决定是否推进。这样新增一个玩法只需要定义并发布它的事件,不需要改动流程代码。叙述序列与步骤之间也不增加额外字段:序列结束时发布"序列已结束"信号,下一个步骤把它作为触发条件,从而把"教学—演出—教学"首尾相连。

针对两类剧情分支,系统同样分开处理：对游戏内容有影响的选择(如是否治疗受伤的龙、是否接受竞速、装备类型)会额外发布"重大选择"事件并写入存档,后续内容据此判断;仅影响对话表现的选择只记录在对话历史中,不触发任何后续逻辑。并且所有路径最终必须汇合到同一个可达状态(例如无论是否参加竞速,最终都会达到龙的第三信任阶段),避免任何分支让玩家无法继续。

为保证流程不被玩家的非预期行为打断,我加入了几项机制:一是步骤进入时先检查世界状态,如果条件已经满足(例如玩家已经下龙)就静默跳过;二是对可能早于步骤出现的事件(如到达某地点)采用周期性重复广播,直到被确认;三是所有等待都设有看门狗超时;四是临时的教学限制统一通过按所有者登记的"能力锁"管理,步骤结束时自动释放,不会残留。

目前章节切换由按固定顺序运行的各幕步骤列表实现,任务显示则依赖采集目标事件与日志中的手写文本。后续计划在现有事件契约上增加章节状态机(支持进入条件、并行任务和最低信任保底)与正式的任务系统,二者只需替换流程的调度组件,不需要修改已完成的教学、对话与玩法内容。

有了关卡系统的架构后，我将游戏内容按照功能分为：采集系统、道具系统、战斗系统、对话系统、环境系统、引导系统。其中战斗系统我参考了类魂游戏的设计，将BOSS放置在地图的指定区域，按照游戏流程设定了出场顺序和动画，战斗中的设计则仿照了类魂的战斗模式和UI表现，例如阶段化，并将这个系统和采集结合，击败敌人后可掉落稀有采集物，提高玩家的战斗成就感，我将这两个系统交给了我的协作者进行开发。而我的主要精力放在环境和引导系统上。

### Level Design

The level system can be considered the core data structure of the entire project. Before starting the coding work, I first went through the full script and identified the entry and exit points of each level. I also designed the individual tasks (objectives) and gameplay for each section, as shown in the image below.

At a high level, the entire game flow can be divided into three types of stages: narrative sequences, tutorials, and player-driven gameplay.

In terms of gameplay, I added branching dialogue choices at selected points during narrative sequences. These choices fall into two categories: those that affect the actual game content, and those that only change the dialogue without affecting subsequent gameplay. Most gameplay takes place during player-driven sections, including resource collection, combat, and sky races.

After breaking down the complete flow into individual events, I listed all the event names in the level design event table, grouped by type. Based on this table, I then abstracted the entire game flow at the code level into three types of containers, corresponding to the three stages described above:

The tutorial stage corresponds to "Steps". Each Step contains a trigger condition, the content to be presented (such as text prompts, button highlights, or narration), a completion condition, and the next Step. Its key characteristic is that it only advances after the player has actually completed the required action. It does not rely on timers, ensuring that the tutorial never moves forward on its own.

The narrative sequence stage corresponds to "Narration Sequences" and "Dialogue". A Narration Sequence is a timeline that progresses over time and can contain instructions such as fades, teleportation, and character animations. Dialogue, on the other hand, uses a node-based structure, with each node containing lines of dialogue, optional branching choices, and the effects of those choices. The distinction between the two is based on who is speaking and where the speech comes from: narration and the protagonist's inner monologue belong to Narration Sequences, while speech from characters who physically exist in the scene belongs to Dialogue.

The player-driven gameplay stage corresponds to "Objectives" and first-time "Beats". Gameplay features such as collection, combat, and racing are implemented independently. They communicate with the flow system only through events, informing it when an objective has been updated or completed. The flow system itself contains no gameplay logic.

These containers do not reference one another directly. Instead, they communicate through a central EventBus. Gameplay modules publish events (such as "player teleported", "item added to inventory", or "enemy defeated"). A signal router translates these events into a unified signal format, which the Step machine subscribes to and uses to determine whether the flow should advance. This means that adding a new gameplay feature only requires defining and publishing its events, without changing the flow code.

The relationship between Narration Sequences and Steps also requires no additional fields. When a sequence ends, it publishes a "sequence ended" signal. The next Step uses this signal as its trigger condition, allowing tutorials and narrative sequences to connect seamlessly.

The two types of narrative choices are also handled separately. Choices that affect gameplay, such as whether to treat the injured dragon, whether to accept a race, or which equipment to use, publish an additional "major choice" event and are saved to the player's save data. Later content can then check these records to determine what happens next. Choices that only affect how dialogue is presented are recorded in the dialogue history and do not trigger any subsequent logic.

All possible paths must eventually converge on a shared reachable state. For example, whether or not the player participates in the race, they will eventually reach the dragon's third Trust stage. This prevents branching choices from leaving the player unable to continue.

To prevent unexpected player behaviour from interrupting the game flow, I introduced several additional mechanisms:

1. World-state checks: When a Step begins, it first checks the current world state. If its conditions have already been met (for example, if the player has already dismounted the dragon), the Step is silently skipped.
2. Repeated event broadcasting: For events that may occur before the corresponding Step begins, such as reaching a particular location, the system broadcasts the event repeatedly at regular intervals until it is acknowledged.
3. Watchdog timeouts: Every waiting operation has a watchdog timeout to prevent the flow from getting stuck indefinitely.
4. Ability locks: Temporary tutorial restrictions are managed through a unified system of owner-registered "ability locks". These are automatically released when the corresponding Step ends, preventing restrictions from accidentally remaining active.

At present, chapter transitions are implemented through a sequence of Act-specific Step lists that run in a fixed order. Task display relies on collection objective events and manually written text in the game log. For future development, I plan to build a chapter state machine on top of the existing event contracts, supporting entry conditions, parallel objectives, and minimum Trust safeguards. I also plan to introduce a formal quest system. Both can be implemented by replacing the flow system's scheduling components, without modifying the existing tutorial, dialogue, or gameplay content.

With the level system architecture in place, I divided the game's content into several functional systems: the collection system, item system, combat system, dialogue system, environment system, and player guidance system.

For the combat system, I took inspiration from Souls-like games. Bosses were placed in designated areas of the map, with their appearance order and animations determined by the game flow. The combat mechanics and UI presentation also followed the Souls-like approach, including a phased boss structure. I further connected the combat and collection systems: defeating enemies could reward players with rare collectible items, giving them a greater sense of achievement from combat.

I assigned the development of these two systems to my collaborators, while I focused most of my efforts on the environment and player guidance systems.

- 地形适配

在我们美术组的成员产出了地图模型后，我先对环境地形做了适配。但这一项工作花费了比预计要长的时间，这是因为在并不平坦的地面上骑乘时，地形检测的问题必须解决。地面骑乘只能让龙水平移动，无法控制高度，它会直接走进山丘，或漂浮在洼地上方。另外，龙在起飞时只会测量一次地面高度，整个过程中都使用这个单一值作为最低和最高高度，以及着落点。这会导致龙直接飞进墙体里，降落时有可能在地面以下或者悬浮在空中。同样的问题也会发生在龙的自主游荡行为上。

因此需要一种统一的方法来检测此时地面在哪里，以及坡度和材质。这应该是一种可被查询的服务。在实现这个方法的过程中，我还犯了一个错误，为了让龙跟随地面高度平滑移动，我设置了一个处于龙正下方的投影，这导致检测和高度调整存在无法避免的时间差，这个方法在斜坡位置会出现严重误差。因此我将目标点调整到龙前方一小段距离的地面时，龙的身体便可以在到达坡面之前开始抬升，最终的动作也不再出现明显的错误。这是因为，真实的四足动物也会以类似的方式行动：它们会提前感知前方的地形，而不是等到地面发生变化后才做出反应。

### Terrain Adaptation

After the art team had finished producing the map models, I began adapting the environment terrain for gameplay. However, this task took longer than expected because I had to solve several terrain detection problems that occurred when riding the dragon over uneven ground.

When moving on the ground, the dragon could only move horizontally, with no control over its height. As a result, it could walk straight into hills or float above depressions in the terrain. There was also a problem during take-off: the dragon only measured the ground height once, at the beginning of the flight, and then used that single value throughout the entire process as its minimum and maximum flight height, as well as its landing point. This could cause the dragon to fly directly into walls or land below the ground or remain floating in mid-air. The same problems also occurred during the dragon's autonomous wandering behaviour.

I therefore needed a unified way to detect the current ground position, slope, and surface material. This needed to be implemented as a queryable service that different systems could access.

During implementation, I also made a mistake. To make the dragon follow changes in ground height smoothly, I initially placed the ground projection directly beneath the dragon. However, this introduced an unavoidable delay between terrain detection and height adjustment, resulting in significant errors on slopes.

I eventually moved the target detection point slightly ahead of the dragon, onto the ground in front of it. This allowed the dragon to begin raising its body before actually reaching the slope, eliminating the obvious movement errors. This also made sense from a biological perspective: real quadrupedal animals behave in a similar way, sensing the terrain ahead of them and adjusting their movements in anticipation, rather than waiting until the ground changes beneath their feet.

- 引导

引导系统的优先级在开发时被我提前了，这是因为阅读剧本后，我发现整个流程包含大约四十项需要玩家理解的信息，更主要的是，所有系统都和引导息息相关。对于一个预计流程最多不能超过一小时的VR游戏来说，可供玩家自行探索验证的空间并不多，因此引导是一个值得投入大量精力的系统。传统的游戏引导形式无非是提示框UI、文本、语音。而对于一个VR叙事游戏来说，需要在尽量不破坏沉浸感和舒适度的前提下，为游戏经验水平各不相同的玩家提供一种普适性方案绝非易事。

因为我们无法预先知道玩家对 VR 的熟悉程度。项目需要通过测试参与者进行评估，而这些参与者可能拥有自己的头显设备，也可能从未佩戴过 VR 设备。玩过其他 VR 游戏的玩家已经知道 Grip 按钮是什么、位于哪里，也知道自己可以低头看到自己的身体。而第一次体验 VR 的玩家则完全不了解这些。

游戏中的几乎所有操作都是通过实际的肢体动作完成的，而不是按下按钮。游戏中包含玩家必须实际握住的缰绳、需要举到嘴边的号角、佩戴在腰间的腰包，以及需要用手指戳击的腕带。每一种交互方式都比按下按钮更加自然，但也更难用语言描述。因为这里不存在一个可以直接说出名称的单一按钮。

玩家也无法舒适地阅读大量文字。VR 的特性限制了我使用大多数传统的游戏指引展示位置。固定在视野中的大段文字可能引起不适，而当玩家骑着一只移动中的动物，在距离森林地面一百米的高空飞行时，也不可能停下来阅读一整段说明文字。

因此，设计目标逐渐变成了：

如何构建一套完整的教程流程，让初学者能够顺利跟随，让有经验的玩家不会感到枯燥，同时又始终不破坏故事的沉浸感？

### Player Guidance

I moved the player guidance system higher up the development priority list. After reading through the script, I realised that the entire game contained around forty pieces of information that players needed to understand. More importantly, every system was closely connected to player guidance. For a VR game with a playtime that was expected to stay within one hour, there would be very little room for players to explore and figure things out on their own. This made guidance a system worth investing a considerable amount of effort in.

Traditional game tutorials generally rely on UI pop-ups, text, or voice instructions. However, for a narrative-driven VR game, providing a solution that works for players with different levels of gaming experience, while preserving immersion and comfort as much as possible, is far from easy.

We could not know in advance how familiar each player would be with VR. The project would be evaluated by test participants, some of whom might own their own headsets, while others might never have worn a VR headset before. Players who had played other VR games would already know what the Grip button was, where to find it, and that they could look down to see their own bodies. First-time VR players, on the other hand, would have no idea about any of this.

Almost all interactions in the game are performed through physical movements rather than button presses. Players need to physically grab the reins, raise a horn to their mouth, take a pouch from their waist, and use their fingers to tap a wristband. Each of these interactions is more natural than simply pressing a button, but also much harder to explain through words. There is no single button with a name that I can simply refer to.

Players also cannot comfortably read large amounts of text. The nature of VR limits where I can place most traditional tutorial instructions. Large blocks of text fixed in the player's field of view can cause discomfort. And when players are riding a moving creature, flying a hundred metres above the forest floor, they cannot exactly stop to read a lengthy set of instructions.

This gradually led me to a central design question:

How could I build a complete tutorial flow that allows beginners to follow along smoothly, keeps experienced players from getting bored, and never breaks the immersion of the story?

value.zh:
单纯一行文字的方案并不可行。对于初学者而言，文字提到了他们根本无法定位的事物。例如“按下 Grip 键”默认玩家知道手指下方的哪个按钮被称为 Grip。“低头看向腰部”默认玩家知道自己拥有一个可以低头看到的虚拟身体。“拿起床头柜上的日志”则默认玩家能够在进入房间十一秒后找到指定物品。对于初学者，尤其是那些对 VR 和电子游戏都不熟悉的玩家来说，他们往往并不具备这些直觉。

对于有经验的玩家而言，同样的文字却变成了一种阻碍。玩过其他 VR 游戏的玩家会本能地使用传送移动。告诉他们如何完成这一操作不仅没有必要，还会拖慢游戏流程，尤其是在他们刚刚开始形成对这款游戏的第一印象时。

在这一阶段，最自然的解决方案似乎是采用分支式设计：询问玩家拥有多少 VR 使用经验，或者提供一个教程难度设置。但由于这种方案会带来过大的开发工作量，我最终放弃了这一做法。此外，对于一种玩家此前几乎没有接触过的媒介，他们可能也很难准确判断自己的实际能力。

我最终采取的方案根据不同问题对引导方式进行分层。每个步骤都可以同时激活多个呈现通道，并且每个通道只负责回答一个问题（如图所示）：

- 触觉反馈（Haptic feedback）：通过即将使用的控制器传递一次震动，回答“用哪只手？”；
- 按钮高亮（Button highlighting）：在控制器模型上直接突出显示对应按钮，回答“按哪个按钮？”；
- 控制器上方的悬浮面板：回答“执行什么操作？”；
- 物体高亮、地面标记或绘制出的手势区域：回答“在哪里操作？”；
- 视野上方边缘附近的一行文字：回答“目标是什么？”；
- 旁白语音（Narrator's voice）：回答“为什么要这样做？”

这种设计能够适应不同玩家的经验差异，因为玩家可以根据自身经验逐层忽略这些引导通道。有经验的玩家只需阅读目标文字、听取操作原因，随后便可以直接行动。触觉反馈、按钮高亮、控制器上方的面板位于视野边缘，不会主动干扰玩家，因此玩家可以自然地忽略它们。

首次体验 VR 的玩家则可以跟随震动定位对应的手，通过发光的按钮找到需要操作的控制键，再借助面板理解具体的操作方式。这两类玩家并不会进入不同的教学步骤，而是从同一个教学步骤中获取不同深度的信息。

这一设计也形成了一条我认为可以应用于任何类似系统的原则：

面板告诉玩家应该使用哪个控制器操作，文字告诉玩家当前的目标是什么。两者绝不能重复传达同一句话。
value.en:
A text-only approach was not sufficient. For beginners, the instructions often referred to things they could not even identify. For example, "Press the Grip button" assumes that players already know which button beneath their fingers is called Grip. "Look down at your waist" assumes that they know they have a virtual body they can look down at. "Pick up the journal on the bedside table" assumes that they can locate the correct object within the eleven seconds after entering the room. Beginners, especially those unfamiliar with both VR and video games, often lack these basic intuitions.

For experienced players, however, the same instructions become an obstacle. Players who have used other VR games will instinctively know how to move using teleportation. Explaining this to them is unnecessary and only slows down the game, particularly when they are just beginning to form their first impression of it.

At this stage, the most obvious solution seemed to be a branching tutorial design: ask players how much VR experience they have, or provide a tutorial difficulty setting. However, I eventually abandoned this approach because it would require too much additional development work. Furthermore, when dealing with a medium that players may have very little experience with, they might not be able to accurately assess their own abilities.

I eventually adopted a layered approach to guidance, using different methods to address different questions. Each tutorial Step can activate multiple presentation channels simultaneously, with each channel responsible for answering just one question, as shown in the image:

- Haptic feedback: Sends a vibration through the controller that the player needs to use, answering "Which hand?"
- Button highlighting: Highlights the corresponding button directly on the controller model, answering "Which button?"
- Floating panel above the controller: Answers "What action should I perform?"
- Object highlighting, ground markers, or drawn gesture areas: Answers "Where should I perform the action?"
- A single line of text near the upper edge of the player's field of view: Answers "What is the objective?"
- Narrator's voice: Answers "Why am I doing this?"

This design accommodates differences in player experience because players can selectively ignore guidance channels based on what they already know. Experienced players only need to read the objective text and listen to the explanation of why they should perform the action before proceeding. Haptic feedback, button highlighting, and the panel above the controller are positioned at the edge of the player's field of view and do not actively interrupt their experience, so they can be ignored naturally.

First-time VR players, on the other hand, can follow the vibration to identify the correct hand, locate the required button through its visual highlight, and then use the panel to understand the specific action they need to perform. These two types of players do not enter different tutorial steps. Instead, they receive different levels of information from the same tutorial Step.

This also led me to a principle that I believe can be applied to any similar system:

The panel tells players which controller to use for an action, while the text tells them what the current objective is. The two should never repeat the same information.

除此之外，我后来还在特定场景中加入了地面标记引导，物体高亮，以及可被玩家感知的触发区视觉引导等。

在引导设计的过程中，我获得了一些珍贵经验。第一，玩家操作应当被拆解为多个步骤。以缰绳操作为例：同时握住两侧把手，等待它们激活，然后将缰绳向胸前拉动。其中握住把手和将缰绳向胸前拉动是两个独立的操作，设计者需要尽可能考虑操作中所有可能的步骤，并设置相应的引导和成败反馈，因为在实际游戏过程中，任何一个独立步骤都可能成为玩家失败的原因。

第二，引导和游戏节奏相结合。尤其对于叙事游戏来说，并不需要单独的引导章节。举例来说：

第一幕（Act 1）的梦境发生在主线故事四年前，玩家在骑龙离家的过程中学习基础移动和地面骑乘。这一设计与叙事自然结合，使教学不再显得独立于故事之外。

第二幕（Act 2）通过抚摸和喂食教授养成机制，并通过一次预设失败引入照料系统：首次骑乘仅几步后，龙便耗尽耐力，玩家随之返回地面。游戏没有直接解释耐力的重要性，而是先让玩家感受到需求，再展示解决方法。

第三幕（Act 3）在 Kelly 修复鞍具、龙的信任度提升后教授飞行。第四幕（Act 4）则在比赛结束、玩家获得攻击能力后，通过蜥蜴人的出现引入战斗教学。

因此，每项教学都在故事提供使用动机之后才出现。教学节奏由叙事决定，而非设计师对玩家信息接收能力的主观估计。
value.en:
In addition, I later added ground markers, object highlighting, and visual guidance for trigger zones that players could recognise in specific scenes.

During the design of the guidance system, I gained some valuable experience.

First, player actions should be broken down into individual steps. Take the reins as an example: players need to grab both handles at the same time, wait for them to activate, and then pull the reins towards their chest. Grabbing the handles and pulling the reins towards the chest are two separate actions. Designers need to consider as many possible steps in an interaction as they can, and provide appropriate guidance and feedback for both success and failure. In actual gameplay, any individual step could be the reason why a player fails to complete an interaction.

Second, guidance should be integrated into the pacing of the game. This is particularly important for narrative-driven games, which do not necessarily need a separate tutorial chapter. For example:

- Act 1: The dream sequence takes place four years before the main story. As players ride the dragon away from home, they learn the basic movement controls and how to ride on the ground. This naturally integrates the tutorial into the narrative, rather than making it feel like a separate part of the game.
- Act 2: Players learn the dragon-care mechanics through petting and feeding. A scripted failure then introduces the care system: after only a few steps during their first ride, the dragon runs out of stamina, forcing the player to return to the ground. Instead of directly explaining why stamina matters, the game first lets players experience the dragon's needs before showing them how to address them.
- Act 3: After Kelly repairs the saddle and the dragon's Trust increases, players are taught how to fly.
- Act 4: After the race ends and players acquire the ability to attack, the appearance of the Lizardmen introduces the combat tutorial.

In this way, each tutorial is introduced only after the story has given players a reason to use the corresponding mechanic. The pacing of the tutorials is determined by the narrative, rather than by the designer's subjective estimate of how much information players can absorb.

value.zh:
这一安排也与第 3.4 节的信任度成长机制相结合：分阶段解锁既体现了玩家与龙的关系发展，也控制了教学节奏，使同一机制同时承担两项相互关联的功能。

实现这一设计的关键是教学锁定机制（Teaching Lock）：在对应课程完成前，暂时禁用相关能力。例如，在飞行教学开始前，起飞功能始终处于锁定状态；在召唤教学前，号角也无法召唤龙。这种机制使引导触发更加可控，避免玩家在预设教学流程之外提前使用能力，导致教学无法触发或故事进程受阻。这一问题在实际测试中经常出现。

另外，还有一个细节的设计决策：我们尽量编写了符合叙事语境的引导文本，让虚拟角色语音的方式来承担引导任务，并且分别对故事人物的字幕和引导文本用不同的UI和字体大小等来表示，避免玩家感到出戏和混淆。

在实现方面，我将引导分为三类，每一类单独一个容器，有不同的结束条件：

1. 步骤：需要玩家完成，完成与否是唯一终止判定。
2. 序列：仅说明，不强制要求玩家必须完成才能推进，随时间自动终止。
3. 节拍：只在某个事件被触发时出现。并非预先设定好的出现时机，需要玩家完成后终止。

这是因为需要引导的情形各不相同，例如，节拍型的引导是为了某些首次出现在游戏里的情况不让玩家感到困惑而设置的。这些类型的完善都是随着游戏的开发进展而逐渐补充，并非一蹴而就。
value.en:
This arrangement also worked together with the Trust progression system described in Section 3.4. Unlocking abilities in stages reflected the development of the relationship between the player and the dragon, while also controlling the pacing of the tutorials. In this way, the same mechanic served two closely related purposes.

The key to implementing this design was the Teaching Lock mechanism, which temporarily disables relevant abilities until the corresponding tutorial has been completed. For example, the take-off ability remains locked until the flight tutorial begins, and the horn cannot summon the dragon before the summoning tutorial. This makes tutorial triggers more controllable and prevents players from using abilities before they are introduced, which could otherwise cause tutorials to fail to trigger or block story progression. This problem occurred frequently during actual testing.

There was also another small but important design decision. We tried to write tutorial instructions that fitted naturally into the narrative context, using the voices of in-game characters to deliver guidance wherever possible. We also used different UI elements and font sizes for character dialogue subtitles and tutorial instructions. This helped prevent players from feeling disconnected from the story or becoming confused about the source of the information.

In terms of implementation, I divided guidance into three types, each with its own container and termination conditions:

1. Step: Requires the player to complete an action. Completion is the only condition for termination.
2. Sequence: Provides information without requiring the player to complete anything before proceeding. It terminates automatically over time.
3. Beat: Appears only when a specific event is triggered. Its appearance time is not predefined, and it terminates once the player has completed the required action.

This separation was necessary because different situations require different types of guidance. For example, Beats are designed to prevent players from feeling confused when they encounter something in the game for the first time. These types and their implementation details were gradually refined as development progressed, rather than being fully established from the beginning.

五、取舍以及迭代

最初的取舍发生在集成环境阶段。当我将场景素材和地图设置导入项目后，在真机上进行的性能测试就暴露了大量的问题。因此，在开展环境优化工作之前，进行性能测试和优化是很有必要的。一旦加入大量会影响性能开销的内容，这会导致性能问题更加难以排查。

为了排查严重的帧率问题，我在头显上开启了实时的性能数据显示，并且通过日志记录每一次的测试结果。我还编写了脚本来帮助我逐项调整可能影响到性能的数据，通过反复实验的方式一一排查，例如在包含大量贴图的地面静止和移动，抬头看向渲染消耗低的天空和消耗高的地面等等。最终，我发现主要影响性能的原因是草地贴图所采用的着色器脚本，从URP/Lit改为自定义的脚本后，主要的性能问题就解决了。但运行时的开销依然偏高，尽管我已经尝试了将各项性能设置调整至可接受范围内的最低，这导致我后面在进行环境优化时，采取了最保守的策略。

## 5. Design Trade-offs and Iteration

The first major trade-off came during environment integration. After importing the scene assets and map settings into the project, performance tests on the actual headset revealed a large number of issues. This made it clear that performance testing and optimisation should take place before starting detailed environment optimisation. Once large amounts of performance-intensive content have been added, it becomes much harder to identify the source of performance problems.

To investigate the severe frame-rate issues, I enabled real-time performance monitoring on the headset and recorded the results of each test in logs. I also wrote a script to help me adjust potentially performance-affecting parameters one by one. Through repeated experiments, I tested different scenarios, such as standing still or moving across terrain with many textures, and looking upwards towards the relatively inexpensive sky or downwards towards the more expensive terrain.

Eventually, I identified the shader used by the grass textures as the main cause of the performance issues. Replacing `URP/Lit` with a custom shader resolved most of the major problems.

However, the runtime performance cost was still relatively high. Even after lowering various performance settings to the minimum acceptable levels, the overall overhead remained significant. As a result, I adopted a much more conservative approach to environment optimisation in the later stages of development.

- 云层

对于环境优化，我首先考虑到的是云层。云层不仅仅是让游戏场景更加真实，而且对于穿过云层飞行的体验也是游戏的一项实际需求。玩家可以从下方任意位置穿过云层，且云层不能让人感觉像一堵墙。从上方仍应能够透过云层看到地形，而穿越云层时的感受应该类似穿过烟雾，而不是突然陷入黑暗。

最直接的方案是使用一组半透明几何体，同时实现远距离的云层视觉效果和玩家进入云层后的包围感。这是一种常见的云层实现方式，但在玩家穿越云层时，几何体会直接出现在面前，多个透明像素层覆盖整个屏幕，带来极高的渲染开销。

此外，为避免几何体与其他物体相交时出现生硬边缘，还需要使用 Soft Particles，而这又需要深度纹理。对于基于 Tile 的移动 GPU，这意味着额外的深度 Pass。在帧耗时已经达到预算三倍的设备上，这种方案无法接受。

设计迭代的关键在于认识到：云层的视觉呈现与玩家身处云层中的感受实际上是两个不同的问题。

进入云层后的感受由雾效实现。项目中所有 Shader 的 Fragment Path 已经集成了引擎雾效，因此每帧调整雾的密度和颜色不会增加 Draw Call，也不会产生额外像素。

远距离看到的云层则由两个随摄像机水平移动的低多边形圆盘实现，使用 Unlit 半透明材质。其开销为两个 Draw Call、约 12,000 个三角形和少量纹理采样。

这一方案能够保持低开销的关键在于：几何体始终不会接近摄像机。 当玩家接近云层时，两个圆盘会在距离玩家数十米的位置逐渐淡出，同时雾效开始增强。因此，几何体不会穿过摄像机的近裁剪面，无需 Soft Particles 或深度纹理，也不会产生昂贵的近距离全屏透明叠加。雾效本身不属于几何体，因此不会产生 Overdraw。

两个层次必须使用同一张覆盖率贴图（Coverage Map）。如果它们采用不同的覆盖范围，玩家可能先看到一小片稀薄的云，进入后却发现云层异常浓密。这种不一致会立即破坏整体视觉效果。

### Clouds

For environment optimisation, the first thing I focused on was the cloud layer. Clouds were not just there to make the game environment look more realistic. Flying through them was also an important part of the gameplay experience. Players needed to be able to enter the clouds from almost any position below, without the clouds feeling like a solid wall. The terrain should still be visible through the clouds from above, and flying through them should feel more like passing through smoke than suddenly being plunged into darkness.

The most straightforward solution was to use a set of transparent geometric meshes to create both the distant appearance of the clouds and the sense of being surrounded by them when the player entered. This is a common approach to cloud rendering. However, when players fly through the clouds, these meshes appear directly in front of the camera. Multiple layers of transparent pixels can cover the entire screen, resulting in a very high rendering cost.

In addition, avoiding hard edges where the geometry intersects with other objects requires the use of Soft Particles, which in turn require a depth texture. On tile-based mobile GPUs, this means an additional depth pass. For a device where frame time was already three times over budget, this approach was simply unacceptable.

The key to the design iteration was recognising that the visual appearance of distant clouds and the feeling of being inside them were actually two separate problems.

The feeling of entering the clouds is created using fog. The Fragment Path of every shader in the project had already been integrated with the engine's fog system. This meant that adjusting the fog density and colour each frame would not increase the number of draw calls or introduce additional pixel rendering costs.

The distant appearance of the clouds, on the other hand, is created using two low-poly discs that move horizontally with the camera, using unlit transparent materials. Their combined rendering cost is just two draw calls, approximately 12,000 triangles, and a small number of texture samples.

The key to keeping this solution lightweight is that the geometry never gets close to the camera. As the player approaches the clouds, the two discs gradually fade out when they are still several dozen metres away, while the fog effect begins to intensify. This prevents the geometry from crossing the camera's near clipping plane. There is no need for Soft Particles or depth textures, and no expensive full-screen transparent overdraw at close range. Since the fog itself is not geometry, it does not introduce overdraw.

Both layers must use the same Coverage Map. If they use different coverage areas, players might first see a thin patch of clouds from a distance, only to discover that the cloud layer is unexpectedly dense when they enter it. This inconsistency would immediately break the overall visual effect.

- 边界

紧接着我很自然就考虑到了边界的处理。玩家既不应该看到世界边界，也不能穿越边界。

最初，我打算通过简单地增加边缘云层的厚度来遮挡边界，但由于几何结构的限制，这一方案并不可行。云层是水平分布的，因此只能遮挡那些向下倾斜并穿过云层的视线。当玩家从地面望向边缘，或以较低高度穿越山谷时，视线接近水平，会直接从云层下方穿过，完全无法被遮挡。

最终方案是降低云层高度。靠近地图边缘时，原本用于形成云层柔和起伏的高度偏移继续向下延伸，同时云层逐渐加厚。玩家看到的不再是头顶的云层，而是一道从地面升起的雾墙。这种效果类似海雾向陆地蔓延的真实天气现象，因此在视觉上也较为合理。同时，由于雾墙从地面延伸至云层高度，可以遮挡各个方向的视线，而不仅仅是向下倾斜的视线。

这一雾墙有两个值得讨论的设计决策。

第一，雾效必须设置最低可见距离，而不只是最高密度。

玩家进入雾墙后，可见距离不能低于约 25 米。这与通常对边界遮挡功能的理解相反。原因在于玩家实际上可以进入雾墙，而浓到足以完全遮挡边界的雾，也可能让玩家失去方向感，无法找到返回的路线。相比之下，一个仍能隐约看见的边界，也好过一个将玩家困住的边界。

第二，边界阻挡采用隐形碰撞体，而不是通过地形实现。

最初的方案是将地形边缘抬高，形成超过龙可攀爬坡度限制的陡坡，从而复用现有系统，以较低成本实现一道“围栏”。但这需要美术人员重新调整地形边缘。随着雾墙承担了隐藏边界的任务，阻挡功能便成为一个纯粹由代码实现的问题。

此外，这里还考虑了 VR 舒适性要求：边界必须逐渐降低玩家的移动速度，绝不能突然将玩家“推”停。

当玩家朝地图边缘飞行时，会先看到雾气逐渐变浓，随后感受到龙开始温和地拒绝继续前进。玩家因此会将其理解为“前方天气恶劣”，而不是“撞上了一堵隐形墙”。

### Boundaries

The next issue I naturally turned to was how to handle the world boundaries. Players should neither be able to see the edge of the world nor pass through it.

My initial idea was to hide the boundaries by simply increasing the thickness of the clouds around the edges. However, this was not feasible due to the limitations of the geometry. The clouds are distributed horizontally, so they can only block lines of sight that angle downwards and pass through them. When players look towards the edge from the ground, or fly through a valley at a relatively low altitude, their line of sight is almost horizontal and passes directly underneath the clouds, leaving the boundaries completely exposed.

The final solution was to lower the cloud layer. Near the edges of the map, the height offset originally used to create the clouds' soft, undulating shape continues further downwards, while the cloud layer gradually becomes thicker. Instead of seeing clouds above their heads, players see a wall of fog rising from the ground. This resembles a real weather phenomenon in which sea fog spreads inland, making the effect visually plausible. More importantly, because the fog wall extends from the ground up to the height of the cloud layer, it can block lines of sight from all directions, rather than only those angled downwards.

There were two design decisions worth discussing regarding this fog wall.

First, the fog effect needed a minimum visibility distance, not just a maximum density.

When players enter the fog wall, their visibility must not drop below approximately 25 metres. This goes against the usual assumption that a boundary should be completely hidden. The reason is that players can actually enter the fog wall. Fog dense enough to completely obscure the boundary could also make players lose their sense of direction and prevent them from finding their way back. A boundary that remains faintly visible is better than one that leaves players trapped.

Second, the boundary uses invisible colliders to block movement, rather than relying on the terrain itself.

My initial approach was to raise the terrain along the map edges, creating slopes steeper than the maximum gradient the dragon could climb. This would allow me to reuse the existing system and create a kind of "fence" at relatively low cost. However, this would require the art team to adjust the terrain around the edges. Once the fog wall took over the task of hiding the boundaries, blocking player movement became a purely code-based problem.

I also had to consider VR comfort: the boundary needed to gradually reduce the player's movement speed, rather than suddenly bringing them to a stop by "pushing" them back.

When players fly towards the edge of the map, they first see the fog gradually becoming thicker. They then feel the dragon gently resisting their attempts to move forward. This encourages them to interpret the situation as "bad weather ahead", rather than as having "hit an invisible wall".

- 变化的天空盒

这是本项目中最值得在未来进一步开发的部分。

故事的后半段讲述了北方发生的战争，以及一场正在世界各地蔓延的腐化。然而，由于游戏流程限制，战争发生在一个玩家永远不会亲自前往的地方，这本身也是后续待开发章节的内容。但环境需要一些明确的表现让玩家感知到世界正在随着故事进展发生变化。

在游戏的大部分时间里，玩家都处于森林上方飞行，四面八方的地平线都没有遮挡。改变天空既不需要新的几何体，也不需要玩家执行任何操作。它是游戏中最直接的视觉叙事元素，同时也是制作成本最低的对象。

因此，天空盒根据叙事进程采用了分阶段设计。第一阶段是蓝天和宁静的小镇。第二阶段，天空转为红色，地平线上出现火光，远处还有炮弹落下。第三阶段则发生在夜晚，炮火和燃烧建筑产生的火光依然存在。各阶段之间采用交叉淡入淡出（Cross-fade），而不是直接切换，因为如果天空突然发生变化，恰好看到这一瞬间的玩家可能会认为这是一个 Bug。

这一设计也与引导系统形成了联系。在第四幕中，受伤的龙被治愈后，会飞到云层上方，旁白要求玩家飞到云层之上进行观察。玩家向上穿过云带，看到的便是已经发生变化的天空。教学、故事节点与环境变化由此成为同一个事件。

这也引出一个实现过程中出现的问题。

分阶段天空盒设计要求远处的小镇始终保持可见，而边界系统的存在恰恰是为了确保玩家无法看到远处的任何内容。两者直接冲突，因此必须解决这一问题。

有两种方案。第一种是削弱朝向小镇一侧的雾墙，并将其表现为距离雾（Distance Fog）。这样做可能会暴露地图边缘，同时还需要美术人员制作能够遮挡地平线的远景几何体。第二种是将整个远景放入天空盒中，放置在地平线之上，同时保留雾墙对地面区域的遮挡。

最终选择了第二种方案，原因有三点。首先，它不会增加任何 Draw Call，因为所有内容都在原本就会执行的天空盒渲染通道（Skybox Pass）中完成。其次，它不需要改动边界系统。第三，它不会产生视差错误：天空盒位于无限远处，因此即使玩家在地图上移动一公里，小镇也不会看起来随着玩家一起移动。

这也引出了一个有用的推论：如果所有远景元素都位于无限远处，那么会移动的远景元素也应该放置在无限远处。烟囱冒出的烟和炮弹留下的轨迹并不是场景中的粒子，而是直接合成到天空盒着色器（Skybox Shader）中的。着色器已经拥有视线方向信息，因此不需要进行 UV 映射。“靠近地平线”可以通过垂直分量判断，而“朝向小镇”则可以通过方位角判断。烟雾只需使用一张限制在该区域内滚动的贴图；炮弹轨迹则使用逐帧动画贴图（Flipbook）；不同阶段之间的过渡则通过混合两个立方体贴图（Cubemap）实现。
